action_summary: python.refactor.rename_symbol.v1 was the top-ranked candidate for "Rename the function line_total to item_total in <b>/app and update every caller" (score 11, three times the next candidate) and never ran: it was dropped on module/new_symbol/run_tests:not_stated. Two independent defects were found and both fixed where they live. (1) The binder refused three keys the repository already declares -- the adapter states its own harness defaults (`args.get(k) or <usable value>`), the sentence states the replacement ("to item_total"), and the tree under the stated source_root states the defining module -- so derive_declared_inputs reads those declarations, only after the pinned and typed binders have both refused a key (a stated value always wins), never derives a REFERENT (code_multilanguage_tree_sitter falls back to source_root or "canonical/runtime", which would index a tree the sentence never named), and binds nothing on a tie. (2) The adapter compared import SPELLINGS as strings: target_mod was the module path relative to source_root ("models") while the caller writes the package prefix ("app.models"), so the caller file produced no edits, no unknown_sites entry, and `complete` still said true. Module identity is now FILE identity -- dotted-segment-suffix resolution onto the parsed file set, honouring `from .` levels -- and the harvest is re-run over the POST-edit trees so a surviving provable reference refuses RESIDUAL_REFERENCE before a byte is written. The registry row's expect was unreachable for the same reason (gate == PASS is emitted only when a named pytest suite ran green), so its contract is now complete == true. Measured: T1_LOCAL fails on c79a8f5 (FAIL__RAW_GOAL_COMPILATION_GAP) and passes here at 338 ms; tiers 1/10 -> 2/10; an honest A/B over fifteen sentences on a pristine HEAD worktree shows exactly one FAIL->PASS and no new pass.
